newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria tightens control ready for currency board.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria tightens control ready for currency board.

text.p: Bulgaria is already functioning under the conditions of a tight monetary regime known as a currency board, caretaker Finance Minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said on Wednesday.

"In March we have worked under the conditions of a currency board. The exchange rate is almost fixed, there has been no central bank lending to the budget and to commercial banks," Gavriiski told reporters.

Bulgaria's interim cabinet pledged to introduce the currency boord in June to restore confidence in its troubled financial system, under a $510 million 14-month International Monetary Fund (IMF) standby accord sealed last month.

The first tranche of the funding would be made available before general elections due on April 19, after the interim cabinet adopts a package of measures that lay the ground for the currency board implementation.
The government is expected to complete the first preparatory steps, which include approving a 1997 budget, before the IMF board meets to consider Bulgarian funding next week.
Speaking before a cabinet meeting dicussing Bulgaria's obligations under the IMF accord, Gavriiski said that most of the short-term targets had been met so far.
The exchange rate has remained steady at around 1,600 levs to the dollar since March 10. The national currency tumbled in February to a record low of 3,000 to the dollar.
Budget revenue has been high and the government has not borrowed from the central bank, said Gavriiski, but declined to elaborate.
He said central bank reserves rose by $100 million in March.
The government said on Tuesday that farm produce prices will be liberalised shortly and other prices are being decontrolled. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
